Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private economics
Security: KMS, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nadarajan (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Helios Head of AI), Marco Rivera (Platform Eng), Anita Singh (Legal), Tomás Oliveira (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, I think we have a tight agenda — quick recap of the perf numbers, align on success criteria, then commercial and legal items. Is that right Laura?
[00:15] Laura: Yep, that works. We just want to make sure the latency and throughput map to our SLA and the economics are clear, we need a clear yes/no by end of month.
[00:30] Priya: I'll start with the numbers we ran last week on the 8-bit quantized model, these are the end-to-end p95s across our sample prompts, note that a couple of the longer prompts have higher variance because of tokenization differences.
[00:50] Priya: p50 around 120ms hosted, p95 around 340ms hosted with 8-bit. Dedicated drops p95 to ~220ms at the same batch size, and private on similar infra sits at about 240ms — small delta due to network/runner config. We also tried an aggressive batching profile, that improved throughput but pushed tail latency up so we wouldn't meet the 300ms p95 target in some cases.
[01:30] Marco: sorry, did you say 120ms p50, 340 p95 — are those with cache enabled? we rely heavily on prefix caching so numbers might be different for us.
[01:40] Priya: Good call — these were without prefix caching to show worst-case cold responses, with our KV prefix cache enabled the p95 drops by roughly 40-60ms depending on hit rate. For Helios we saw a simulated 65% hit rate which maps to p95 ~260 on hosted and ~200 on dedicated.
[02:10] Laura: OK that's helpful. The business bar is p95 <= 300ms for primary flows and cost per 1M tokens should be under $400 for the pilot economics, otherwise our finance won't sign.
[02:30] Jordan: Noted, we'll map the final price band to that threshold. We have three options: hosted API trial, dedicated reserved pool, or private deployment (VPC) — each with tradeoffs on cost and control.
[03:00] Tomás: From product's perspective, we need predictable latency and the ability to roll back to a cheaper model if quality regresses. How do rollouts look in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:20] Priya: Same rollout primitives across all deployments — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to model variant. In Dedicated you also get stricter capacity guarantees which makes the rollback behavior more predictable because you aren't subject to multitenant noisy neighbors. But going Private gives you the most control over networking and KMS.
[03:50] Marco: One of our concerns is KMS integration and audit log retention. Anita, do we need something special here?
[04:05] Anita: We need to confirm KMS integration patterns and that the logs meet our SOC-2 policy, also data residency in EU for certain records. We can't sign until legal confirms those artifacts.
[04:25] Jordan: We'll send a KMS integration guide and the audit log schema; Priya will include expected retention options.
[04:40] Priya: Also to call out the quantization tuning we did — for your dataset we had to relax one layer's weight clipping to maintain coherence on long prompts, that increased cost slightly but improved rouge-like metrics on internal evals.
[05:10] Laura: Can you quantify "slightly"? Finance needs delta to compare to current spend.
[05:20] Priya: On average cost went up ~6% compared to the most aggressive 4-bit profile, but latency improved 12% and quality improved on our chat eval by 4 points.
[05:40] Marco: Is that visible in the dashboard? we want to see token-level breakdowns.
[05:50] Jordan: Yes, Console will show per-route token cost and latency — we'll share a snapshot filtered to your routes.
[06:00] [06:00] Jordan: (quick cross-talk as Laura types)
[06:15] Laura: One important success criteria is 7-day data retention for logs in the pilot, but production will need longer, so the POC shouldn't rule out that requirement.
[06:30] Priya: For the pilot we can enable 7-day retention in the hosted trial; Dedicated and Private can be configured for longer retention as needed.
[06:45] Tomás: On the timeline — if we run a short on-prem baseline the week of 11/25, and if that looks good, when do you expect we could switch to Dedicated?
[06:55] Jordan: Contracting is the usual path — if Helios signs a reserved capacity commit, Dedicated could be provisioned within 4–6 weeks from commitment; Private longer depending on ops. The goal would be to have commercial terms in place by early December.
[07:20] Anita: Are there any third-party partners who will see our data? we need to be clear for the contract.
[07:30] Jordan: No, for Dedicated and Private we don't share customer data with third parties; hosted is multitenant but data is logically separated. We'll include language in the contract and scope the KMS obligations.
[07:50] Marco: On perf tests — what infra spec did you use for these runs? we need to compare to our on-prem nodes.
[08:05] Priya: Tests used A100 80GB equivalent nodes with 1 replica; we'll provide the exact kernel/cuda versions and the runner config so you can match.
[08:30] Laura: We noticed some missed entity cases in the sample eval — did Redwood do any calibration on our prompt templates?
[08:40] Priya: We ran a light prompt reformat to standardize the system message and tokenization, but we didn't change the core prompt logic. We can push a few tuned prompt templates to reduce hallucinations, that was part of the 4% quality bump.
[09:05] Laura: Good — we want to keep the prompt changes minimal so product behavior stays stable.
[09:20] Jordan: Quick commercial note — for pilot there's a standard pilot credit and then three pricing bands: pay-as-you-go (hosted), reserved (dedicated), and enterprise license (private). We'll put concrete numbers in the summary email.
[09:40] Tomás: For decision-making we need two things: one, a run on our infra to confirm p95 with our real QPS; two, final price sheet mapped to our expected monthly token volume.
[10:00] Jordan: Agreed. Priya can run the on-prem baseline with your infra team — Marco, can you share access details and sample traffic pattern?
[10:12] Marco: Yes, will send the access and a traffic spec by tomorrow.
[10:20] [10:20] (several participants typing)
[10:35] Priya: I'll also attach traces and a short guide to reproduce the perf tests. We'll coordinate a 60-minute run window with you.
[10:50] Anita: On legal, we need to see the KMS integration doc and a redlineable contract within the week. We're not asking for anything out of the ordinary but must ensure the residency clause is explicit.
[11:05] Jordan: We'll send the contract template and a security pack.
[11:12] Laura: One more thing: can Redwood guarantee no model parameter exfil? we need assurance on model weights staying private and on inference telemetry.
[11:25] Priya: We can provide an architecture diagram showing where parameters live and the telemetry hooks; for Private deployments all model files remain in your VPC, for Dedicated we have guarded storage with restricted access. We'll call out telemetry fields.
[11:45] Tomás: OK that's great. On the success criteria checklist — can we read it out and confirm?
[11:55] Laura: Sure — p95 <= 300ms for primary flows, pilot cost under $400 per 1M tokens, no data exfil risk, KMS + audit logs validated, and business flow accuracy >= baseline +2% on our eval suite.
[12:20] Jordan: I have that down: (1) p95 <= 300ms, (2) cost < $400/1M tokens, (3) security items cleared, (4) accuracy improvement >= 2%. Anything to add?
[12:35] Anita: Add legal review completed.
[12:40] Jordan: Noted.
[13:00] Laura: Sounds good. If Helios signs off on those, what's the recommended path? Dedicated now with option to migrate to Private?
[13:15] Jordan: Yes that is the standard path — Dedicated gives you reserve capacity and predictability with the option to go Private for stricter networking. We'll include migration playbook in the docs.
[13:35] Marco: Also want to confirm fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity is impacted do we get auto-fallback to hosted model and what are SLAs?
[13:50] Priya: You can opt into auto-fallback; there's a documented SLO for fallbacks and we can set a prioritized region/variant to minimize functional impact.
[14:05] Tomás: Perfect.
[14:20] Jordan: To close, recap of owners and dates: Jordan sends pricing + contract by 11/24, Priya sends perf traces and tuned quant profile by 11/22, Marco provides infra access by 11/21, Anita reviews legal and data residency by 11/26. Any objections?
[14:45] Anita: None, just we need enough time for review.
[15:00] Laura: No objections. Please include a short executive one-pager for our CFO.
[15:15] Jordan: Will do.
[15:30] Laura: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the baseline next week.
[15:40] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with the attachments.
[41:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has typical Fireflies artifacts — occasional mislabels and minor stutters. References to deck and security pack will be attached in follow-up email.
